Ideal rocksalt structural model following Roth (1958), Introduction and Fig. 1; conventional Fm-3m cell with four Ni and four O. The reference edge is normalized to Campbell Table 1 V0, not claimed as a separate ambient cubic refinement. Roth establishes cubic paramagnetic NiO and a rhombohedral distortion below the Neel temperature (523 K at ambient pressure). Campbell reports B1 and fits one cubic-average volume model, including low-temperature MAP points; this record cannot predict magnetic ordering, rhombohedral splitting, or the pressure-dependent Neel boundary. Use the separate nickel\_oxide rhombohedral card for resolved low-temperature diffraction.

295 K BM3 + Mie-Grüneisen-Debye (Equation (5)), no electronic or anharmonic pressure; molar V0 stored per Z = 4 cell. One cubic-average B1 volume model, also fitted to low-temperature points; it cannot predict magnetic ordering, rhombohedral splitting or the pressure-dependent Néel boundary (523 K at ambient pressure). Use the rhombohedral NiO material for resolved low-temperature diffraction.

## Observation datasets

### ni\_nio\_campbell\_2009\_table\_s3\_pvt

- **Description:** All 101 paired fcc-Ni/B1-NiO observations, including nine quenched DAC rows, with NaCl calibration readings and every reported uncertainty.

- **Notes:** Full stored precision, source row order, and all uncertainties are retained. Rows 100-108 are quenched 293-295 K DAC states; Section 2.2 cautions that residual stress invalidates mechanical equilibrium after quenching. The primary refit excludes those nine rows transparently and reports an all-row sensitivity fit. The authors report B1 NiO throughout; the cubic-average volume model does not resolve the low-temperature rhombohedral/magnetic distortion.
